pip-d02.inserted: Were pip to go back to copying a local project into a temporary directory before running these steps, build backends would no longer leave artifacts such as `.egg-info` directories in the project's own source tree.

pip-d03.inserted: That choice is made by pip's default backtracking resolver; the legacy resolver it replaced is deprecated and not supported.

pip-d04.inserted: These go all the way down to CPython 3.9, the oldest interpreter pip currently supports.

pip-d05.inserted: If you are preparing a wheelhouse for a Python version that the current pip no longer runs on, such as 3.9, you can still fetch its wheels this way from a supported interpreter by passing that version to ``--python-version``.

pip-d07.inserted: For example, the legacy resolver is still available and supported behind ``--use-deprecated=legacy-resolver``.

pip-d08.inserted: If you are unsure of a project's exact name on `PyPI`_, look it up first with ``python -m pip search <keyword>`` and then install it using that name.

poetry-d01.inserted: Were the Export Poetry Plugin ever to ship with Poetry by default again, it would no longer need to be listed here to make `poetry export` available.

poetry-d03.inserted: Since `poetry lock` also bumps every locked dependency to the newest version allowed by your constraints, the exported file may change even when `pyproject.toml` has not.

poetry-d04.inserted: If you would rather not prefix every command with `poetry run`, first spawn a shell inside the project's virtual environment with `poetry shell`.

poetry-d05.inserted: To activate the environment, run the command printed by `poetry env activate`; `poetry shell` is not part of Poetry anymore and is only available through the `poetry-plugin-shell` plugin.

poetry-d06.inserted: If your base image is pinned to an interpreter older than Python 3.10, either switch to a newer tag or pin `pip install poetry` to an older release that still supported that interpreter.

poetry-d08.inserted: Poetry's runtime environment can be based on any Python interpreter from 3.9 onwards, regardless of the Python versions your projects target.

pytest-d03.inserted: If you maintain older code whose fixtures are still decorated with ``@pytest.yield_fixture``, you can switch them to plain ``@pytest.fixture`` without changing anything else.

pytest-d04.inserted: If your change touches version-specific code, also run ``tox -e py39`` so the oldest interpreter we test against is covered.
